stem: The height $H$, in metres, of mature trees of a certain variety is normally distributed with standard deviation 0.67. In order to test whether the population mean of $H$ is greater than 4.23, the heights of a random sample of 200 trees are measured.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write down suitable null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The sample mean height, $\bar{h}$ metres, of the 200 trees is found and the test is carried out. The result of the test is to reject the null hypothesis at the 5% significance level.
parts.text: Find the set of possible values of $\bar{h}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Ajit said, ‘In **(b)** we had to assume that $\overline{H}$ is normally distributed, so it was necessary to use the Central Limit Theorem.’

Explain whether you agree with Ajit.
